name: Omni Mount Washington Resort
positioning: Grand resort hotel, officially Omni Mount Washington Resort & Spa, with a history dating to 1902 and Spanish Renaissance architecture, set in New Hampshire's White Mountains
best_for: Golfers and skiers who want a year-round mountain resort
Families looking for summer and winter activities
Travelers drawn to historic grand hotels

facts.text: The resort is in New Hampshire's White Mountains.
The resort features Spanish Renaissance architecture.
The hotel's history stretches back to 1902.
The hotel has a red roof.
The resort has an indoor pool, an outdoor pool and a hot tub.
The resort has two championship golf courses.
Guests can take a zipline canopy tour.
Resort activities include scenic gondola rides, hiking and lawn games.
The resort has red clay tennis courts.
The Cave is a prohibition-era speakeasy tucked within the hotel.
Presidential rooms include access to the Presidential Club lounge, with a daily continental breakfast and afternoon refreshments and snacks.
The resort offers family-friendly activities in both summer and winter.

highlights.text: The hotel's porch looks out over the woodlands of White Mountain National Forest and makes a perch for watching the fall foliage change color.
Noteworthy past guests include Thomas Edison and three US presidents.
One of the resort's championship golf courses was designed by Donald Ross.
The nature-inspired, full-service spa and wellness center covers 25,000 square feet and is open year-round.
Winter brings alpine and Nordic skiing, snowboarding and sleigh rides.

considerations.text: The closest airport is Manchester-Boston Regional, approximately 105 miles or 2 hours away.
A $45 resort fee applies; it covers in-room Wi-Fi, the resort shuttle and access to the fitness center and pools.
Self and valet parking carry a nightly charge.

sources.title: Conde Nast Traveler: Omni Mount Washington Resort
